scenes.line1: Why do some UI tests fail randomly?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why your UI tests sometimes fail for no clear reason? Could timing be the culprit?

scenes.label: Playwright
scenes.sub: Waits for elements to be ready by default.
scenes.say: Playwright waits for elements to be ready before interacting, so you rarely need manual waits.

scenes.label: Selenium
scenes.sub: Needs manual waits for dynamic content.
scenes.say: Selenium expects you to add explicit waits, especially when dealing with dynamic or slow-loading elements.
Playwright handles most waits for you, which means fewer flaky tests. Selenium needs you to handle waits yourself, so timing bugs are more common.
In Playwright, you just click and it waits for you. In Selenium, you need to write extra code to wait for the button to appear before clicking.

scenes.question: Is auto-waiting always enough?
scenes.wrong: Yes, auto-waiting solves all timing issues.
scenes.right: No, sometimes you still need explicit waits for complex async updates.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this: auto-waiting is great, but for complex asynchronous scenarios, you'll still need explicit waits.
